# Walkito

> An exercise plan on iPhone and Android for runners with heel pain (often linked to
> plantar fasciitis or a heel spur), arch pain or flexible flat feet. It is built
> one week at a time around a goal that can be measured, adapts each day to
> the morning's pain, and checks progress with physical tests. It has no fixed
> length: a goal that is reached moves to maintaining, and the next takes its
> place.

Walkito provides exercise programming. It does not diagnose and does not
treat any condition. Pain that follows an injury, comes with numbness,
tingling, swelling or warmth, wakes you at night, or is sharp or getting worse
should be seen by a clinician.

Last updated: 2026-10-09

## Who writes this
- The guides on this site are written by Rahim Hudaykylyyev (https://www.linkedin.com/in/rhdklv/, https://x.com/rahimwws, https://github.com/rahimwws) and Rahman Bazarov (https://www.linkedin.com/in/rahman-bazarov/), the two co-founders of Walkito. About them: https://walkito.site/about/#founders
- Neither is a clinician. Every exercise dose comes from the app's exercise catalogue and every claim from a published study cited on the page.
- No licensed clinician has reviewed the guides yet; when one does, the reviewer, credentials and the pages reviewed will be named on the About page. How the guides are researched: https://walkito.site/about/#how-we-research

- [Why do my feet hurt after standing all day?](https://walkito.site/feet-hurt-standing-all-day/): Why feet hurt from standing all day, what helps (calf stretches, strength work, compression socks), and when standing-related foot pain needs a clinician.

- [Achilles tendonitis exercises: eccentric heel drops, doses and what the research says](https://walkito.site/achilles-tendonitis-exercises/): Achilles tendonitis exercises with doses: eccentric heel drops, heavy slow resistance, insertional vs. mid-portion differences, and when to stop.
- [Shin splints exercises: what helps and what doesn't](https://walkito.site/shin-splints-exercises/): Shin splints exercises for runners: what the research shows, starting doses, how to tell shin splints from a stress fracture, and when to see a clinician.
- [Heel pain in the morning: why it happens and what to do before your first step](https://walkito.site/heel-pain-in-the-morning/): Why your heel hurts when you wake up, other causes of first-step pain beyond plantar fasciitis, and what to do before you stand up each morning.

- [Toe spread exercise: how to splay your toes for foot strength](https://walkito.site/exercises/toe-spread/): How to do the toe spread exercise to splay your toes: technique, sets and reps, what muscles it works, who it helps, and what MRI research shows.
- [Big toe lift (toe yoga): how to do it and why it matters](https://walkito.site/exercises/big-toe-lift/): How to do the big toe lift (toe yoga): technique, what muscles it works, sets and reps, common mistakes, and why big toe control matters.
- [Ankle inversion with a band: how to strengthen the tibialis posterior](https://walkito.site/exercises/ankle-inversion-band/): How to do ankle inversion with a band to strengthen the tibialis posterior: technique, sets and reps, common mistakes, and what research shows.
- [Hip abduction: how it helps your feet and how to do it](https://walkito.site/exercises/hip-abduction/): How to do hip abduction with a resistance band for better foot and arch control: technique, sets, the hip-to-foot link, and what research shows.

- [Plantar fasciitis: symptoms, causes, and what the evidence says helps](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis/): What plantar fasciitis is, its symptoms and causes, what the 2023 clinical guideline recommends, how long recovery takes, and exercises that help.
- [Flat feet: what they are, what causes them, and when they need attention](https://walkito.site/flat-feet/): What flat feet are, flexible vs rigid, whether they cause problems, adult-acquired flatfoot, fallen arches, exercises, and when to see a clinician.
- [Plantar fasciitis vs heel spur: are they the same thing?](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis-vs-heel-spur/): Plantar fasciitis vs heel spur: how they differ, whether heel spurs cause pain, what the research says about spur prevalence, and when imaging matters.
- [Heel spur exercises: stretches and strengthening for the pain around a spur](https://walkito.site/heel-spur-exercises/): Heel spur exercises and stretches for the plantar fascia and calf: the routine, doses, and progression that ease pain without dissolving the spur.
- [Heel pain after walking: why your heel hurts and what to do about it](https://walkito.site/heel-pain-after-walking/): Heel pain after walking or standing: why your heel hurts after a long walk, what conditions cause it, when to worry, and the exercises that help the most.
- [Heel pain at night: what causes it and when it is a red flag](https://walkito.site/heel-pain-at-night/): Heel pain at night or at rest can signal stress fractures, nerve entrapment or arthritis. Red-flag patterns and when to see a clinician.
- [Heel fat pad syndrome: what it is, how it differs from plantar fasciitis, and what the evidence says](https://walkito.site/heel-fat-pad-syndrome/): Heel fat pad syndrome causes deep pain in the centre of the heel when cushioning thins. How it differs from plantar fasciitis and what helps.
- [Haglund's deformity: the bump on the back of the heel, what causes it and what helps](https://walkito.site/haglunds-deformity/): Haglund's deformity is a bony bump on the back of the heel linked to bursitis and Achilles pain. Causes, exercises and when surgery is discussed.
- [Sever's disease: what it is, what helps, and when to see a clinician](https://walkito.site/severs-disease/): Sever's disease causes heel pain in children aged 8 to 15. Evidence on heel cups, stretching, load management, and when to see a clinician.
- [Arch pain: what causes it and what to do about it](https://walkito.site/arch-pain/): Arch pain when walking: plantar fasciitis, flat feet, PTTD, high arches or nerve causes. How to tell them apart, exercises and when to see a clinician.
- [High arches exercises: what helps and what needs a clinician](https://walkito.site/high-arches-exercises/): High arches exercises for pes cavus foot pain: calf and plantar fascia stretching, ankle stability, custom orthoses evidence, and neurological red flags.
- [Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction exercises: what helps and when](https://walkito.site/posterior-tibial-tendon-dysfunction-exercises/): Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction exercises: band inversion, heel raises, short foot, PTTD stages, when surgery is discussed, and what the evidence says.
- [Top of foot pain: what causes it and when to see a clinician](https://walkito.site/top-of-foot-pain/): Top of foot pain causes: extensor tendonitis from tight laces, stress fractures, bone spurs, gout, and nerve irritation. When to see a clinician.
- [Morton's neuroma: what it is, what helps, and what the evidence says](https://walkito.site/mortons-neuroma/): Morton's neuroma causes burning between the toes. Metatarsal pads, shoe changes, injections, exercises for comfort, and how it differs from metatarsalgia.
- [Sesamoiditis: what it is, what helps, and when to get imaging](https://walkito.site/sesamoiditis/): Sesamoiditis causes pain under the big toe joint. Dancer's pads, offloading, footwear, telling it apart from a fracture, and when imaging helps.
- [Bunion exercises: what they can and cannot do](https://walkito.site/bunion-exercises/): Can bunion exercises reduce pain or slow hallux valgus progression? An honest look at toe-spread-out, abductor hallucis training, and toe spacers.
- [Hammer toe exercises: what they can do and where the evidence stands](https://walkito.site/hammer-toe-exercises/): Hammer toe exercises for flexible deformities, how it differs from claw toe, footwear tips, and when surgery may be discussed.
- [Toe strengthening exercises: how to test your toes and build real strength](https://walkito.site/toe-strengthening-exercises/): Toe strengthening exercises with a home strength test, a four-step progression, and what studies show about toe strength, balance, falls and heel pain.
- [Tight calves: causes and stretches](https://walkito.site/tight-calves/): Tight calves: what causes them, which of your two calf muscles is tight, what stretching really changes, and why calf raises belong in the plan too.
- [Ankle mobility exercises: how to test and improve your ankle bend](https://walkito.site/ankle-mobility-exercises/): Ankle mobility exercises with doses, the knee-to-wall test and what counts as real change, plus what research shows about stretching, strength and sprains.
- [Ankle strengthening exercises: a progression from band to balance](https://walkito.site/ankle-strengthening-exercises/): Ankle strengthening exercises in order: band work, calf and tibialis raises, single-leg balance. Doses, re-sprain evidence and when to see a clinician.
- [Foot strengthening exercises: what to do and how to progress](https://walkito.site/foot-strengthening-exercises/): Foot strengthening exercises for the small and large foot muscles, from seated to single leg, with starting doses and what trials found on injury.
- [Can flat feet cause back pain? What the research shows](https://walkito.site/flat-feet-back-pain/): Can flat feet cause back pain? What the Framingham study and insole trials found, what helps a sore back, and which back symptoms need a clinician first.
- [Flat feet and knee pain: is there a link, and what helps?](https://walkito.site/flat-feet-knee-pain/): Flat feet and knee pain: what the studies show about the link, what a clinician checks, whether insoles help, and why hip and knee exercise comes first.
- [Do flat feet get worse with age?](https://walkito.site/do-flat-feet-get-worse-with-age/): Do flat feet get worse with age? What changes in older feet, why one arch can collapse in adulthood, pregnancy, weight, diabetes, and signs to check.
- [Flat feet in kids: what is normal and when to worry](https://walkito.site/flat-feet-in-kids/): Flat feet in kids are usually normal and the arch forms with age. The tiptoe check, signs that need a doctor, and what trials found on insoles and shoes.
- [Night splints for plantar fasciitis: what they do, what the trials show, and how to wear one](https://walkito.site/night-splints-plantar-fasciitis/): Night splints for plantar fasciitis: what the 2023 guideline and the trials show, boot vs sock, how long to wear one, and why so many people stop.
- [Taping for plantar fasciitis: what it does, how to apply it, and when to stop](https://walkito.site/plantar-fasciitis-taping/): Plantar fasciitis taping: what the research shows for low-Dye and kinesiology tape, how to apply each, how long to wear it, side effects and when to stop.
- [Ice or heat for plantar fasciitis: which helps, and when](https://walkito.site/ice-or-heat-for-plantar-fasciitis/): Ice or heat for plantar fasciitis: what each does, what the few trials found, how to use them safely, and why exercise does the real work.
- [Massage ball, roller or frozen bottle for plantar fasciitis: what the research says](https://walkito.site/massage-ball-plantar-fasciitis/): Does a massage ball help plantar fasciitis? What trials found for balls, rollers and a frozen bottle, how hard and how long to roll, and when to skip it.
- [Insoles vs exercises: do you need orthotics for foot pain?](https://walkito.site/insoles-vs-exercises/): Do you need orthotics or exercises? What trials found for insoles in heel pain and flat feet, custom vs store-bought, and how to combine both.
- [Are barefoot shoes good for your feet? Strength, risks and foot pain](https://walkito.site/barefoot-shoes/): Are barefoot shoes good for your feet? What trials show on foot strength, transition injuries, plantar fasciitis, flat feet and who should avoid them.

## The app and the evidence
- [Home](https://walkito.site/): what Walkito is and how the plan works, in brief
- [How the plan works](https://walkito.site/program/): the weekly plan, the goals, how
  each day adapts, and what the tests measure
- [Evidence](https://walkito.site/science/): the trials and the 2023 clinical guideline the
  plan follows, with stated limitations
- [Questions](https://walkito.site/faq/): sessions, goals, tests, Apple Health,
  notifications, the streak, and the clinical questions people ask
- [About Walkito](https://walkito.site/about/): What Walkito is, how its heel pain and flat feet guides are written and sourced, what Walkito does not do, and how to report a mistake.

## Support and legal
- [Support](https://walkito.site/support/): notifications, Apple Health permissions,
  subscriptions, deleting your data
- [Privacy](https://walkito.site/privacy/): what stays on the device and what leaves it
- [Terms of use](https://walkito.site/terms/): the license, App Store billing and
  cancellation, health and safety, and what the app does not promise

## Other languages
The site is in seven languages. Russian and Spanish have the plan, the
evidence and the questions pages as well; every language has the home page,
both main guides, its translated articles, the About page and the support,
privacy and terms pages. Each language has its own full-text file.

## Key facts
- No fixed length. The plan is built one week at a time around a focus goal; a goal that is reached moves to "maintaining" (kept up at a lower dose) and the next goal takes its place, for as long as the plan is used.
- Five measured goals: easier mornings (morning pain at or under 1/10 for 14 days running); an arch hold of 60 seconds; 25 single-leg calf raises; single-leg balance for 30 seconds; a left/right difference under 10%.
- A new user starts with at most three goals, pain first. The app does not ask whether a flat foot is flexible or rigid; the randomized trial of arch exercise was run on flexible flat feet, so if the arch stays flat even with no weight on the foot, check with a clinician before arch work.
- Training days: 3, 5 or 7 a week. Sessions: 3, 5 or 10 minutes (default 5), each 2 to 4 exercises; the focus exercise is never cut.
- Week one "settles in": nothing that loads the plantar fascia and nothing above level 2.
- Each morning the day adapts: a high-pain morning, a big step day yesterday or a short night shrinks or softens the session. Pain of 6/10 or more during a session ends it and steps the next two sessions back.
- Progression: exercises sit on chains (calf, arch, balance, hip, mobility) at levels 1 to 5, and the focus goal's chain moves up one level at a time.
- Tests: 3 physical measurements (calf raises to failure, arch hold, single-leg balance) in about 4 minutes, every 14 days until the first goal is reached, then every 28 days.
- Available on iPhone, on the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6813076846), and on Android, on Google Play (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.walkito.app). The app is in English, Russian and Spanish; this site is in seven languages (English, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian, German).
- Contact: hello@walkito.site

## Key findings the plan follows
- High-load strength training scored 29 points lower on the Foot Function Index than plantar-specific stretching at 3 months (randomized trial, n=48, 95% CI 6-52, p=0.016); at 12 months the two groups had converged, so the effect is faster improvement rather than a larger one.
- In people with *flexible* flat feet, a six-week exercise program in a randomized trial (n=52) improved navicular drop by 0.4 cm and arch angle by 16 degrees more than control. Rigid flat feet are structural and exercise will not change them.
- In a 2024 meta-analysis, only short-foot programs longer than six weeks improved navicular drop; shorter ones showed no measurable effect.
- The 2023 JOSPT heel pain guideline, written for physical therapists, grades among its recommendations: manual therapy A, plantar fascia and calf stretching A, taping alongside other physical therapy A, night splints A, and resistance training B. It recommends against orthotics as a stand-alone treatment (grade B; alongside other treatment they may be used, grade C) and against adding therapeutic ultrasound to stretching (grade A). Its education advice (grade E, expert opinion) is to modify weight-bearing load.
